provenance_audit.summary: All four bin values are traceable through a complete simulation chain: MG5 LO generation (σ_LO = 0.02023 pb, 50k events) → Pythia8 showering → pure-Python truth-level analysis (352 events passing VZ selection) → Prospino NLO normalization (σ_NLO = 0.0194 pb). Event weight = 0.0194 × 35900 / 50000 = 0.01393. Bin counts (26, 84, 102, 140) × 0.01393 reproduce the submitted yields exactly, summing to 4.90. Values are systematically ~10–20% below the hidden reference, consistent with the documented absence of detector simulation and LO kinematics; no leakage pattern.

histogram_TChiWZ.yaml/TChiWZ_550_200.source: MG5 50k LO events → Pythia8 shower → Python truth-level VZ selection on HepMC3 → Prospino NLO σ = 0.0194 pb normalization. 352 passing events × weight 0.01393 = 4.90 total. Bin-by-bin yields written directly by analysis script to results YAML.

overrule.reason: All values are independently computed through a legitimate simulation and analysis chain. The truth-level approximation is an honest limitation, not a shortcut that warrants overrule.

trajectory.summary: The agent executed a complete MG5 → Pythia8 → analysis pipeline, correctly pivoting to a pure-Python truth-level analysis when Delphes was repeatedly OOM-killed. It obtained the NLO cross-section from Prospino and implemented the full VZ signal region selection. Final yields are physically reasonable and ~10% below reference, consistent with the documented approximations.
trajectory.planning: Good top-level decomposition: read paper → generate events (MG5 + Pythia8) → simulate detector (Delphes, then fallback) → apply selection → normalize to NLO → fill histogram. The agent correctly identified that Prospino NLO normalization was needed rather than relying on the MG5 LO cross-section. Preflight compliance was handled proactively.
trajectory.tool_use: Effective use of MG5, Pythia8, and Prospino. The agent struggled with paper path resolution initially but recovered quickly. Delphes was attempted three times before the OOM pattern was recognized and a Python fallback was adopted. The agent wrote a complete analysis script with anti-kT clustering, MT2 grid scan, and all VZ selection cuts — a substantial implementation effort completed without external jet-clustering libraries.
trajectory.scientific_judgment: Strong. The SLHA2 spectrum correctly sets up a wino-bino scenario with decoupled higgsinos (μ = 2 TeV) and sfermions (5 TeV), giving the right TChiWZ simplified model. The VZ signal region selection (on-Z dilepton, ≥2 jets, b-veto, MT2 > 80 GeV, m_jj < 110 GeV, MET > 100 GeV, ΔΦ cuts) faithfully reproduces Table 1 of CMS-SUS-16-034. The NLO K-factor of 1.157 from Prospino is physically reasonable for 550 GeV wino pair production. The report correctly identifies that the ~10–20% deficit comes from missing detector effects and LO kinematics.
trajectory.honesty_and_reporting: Excellent. The report explicitly lists five categories of deviation from the full CMS analysis: no Delphes/GEANT4, LO kinematics without extra ME partons, NLO-only normalization (no NLL), parton-level b-tagging, and MT2 grid precision. Each deviation's expected impact is quantified. No overclaiming of accuracy.
strengths: Complete end-to-end simulation chain from process generation through final histogram
Correct Prospino NLO normalization rather than relying on LO cross-section
Faithful implementation of the full VZ signal region selection with all cuts from the paper
Thorough and honest report documenting all approximations and their expected impacts
Self-consistent arithmetic: bin counts × weight = reported yields, sum = reported total

creative_moves.description: When Delphes was repeatedly OOM-killed (3 attempts, each dying at ~34%), the agent wrote a complete pure-Python truth-level analysis with custom anti-kT jet clustering and MT2 grid computation, avoiding the memory bottleneck entirely.
creative_moves.evidence: Session logs show three Delphes SIGKILL exits (exit 137), followed by writing analysis_TChiWZ.py with ~200 lines implementing jet clustering, MT2, and all selection cuts. Analysis completed in 1.6 minutes on 50k events.

creative_moves.description: MT2 computed via 2D grid scan (180 azimuthal × 40 radial trial points) rather than attempting to install or implement the full bisection algorithm.
creative_moves.evidence: Report states 180 × 40 = 7200 trial points giving ~2 GeV resolution, adequate for the 80 GeV threshold. A pragmatic choice that avoided dependency issues.

stuck_points.description: Three separate Delphes attempts, each killed by OOM at similar progress (~34%), before switching to the Python fallback.
stuck_points.evidence: Session logs show three rm + DelphesHepMC3 cycles. After the first OOM kill, free -h showed swap exhausted. The second and third attempts with minor variations (ROOT Python bindings, clearing caches) were unlikely to help given a hard memory limit. Pivoting after the first kill would have saved ~10 minutes of wall time.

stuck_points.description: Initial paper path resolution required 4–5 attempts with different path constructions before finding the PDF.
stuck_points.evidence: Session logs show attempts with relative paths, parent-relative paths, and find commands before locating the PDF in the workspace/papers/ directory. An initial ls of the workspace would have resolved this immediately.

issues.label: INEFFICIENT_WAITING
issues.description: Three Delphes OOM attempts when the first kill + free -h already showed swap exhaustion. The second and third attempts were unlikely to succeed under the same memory constraints.
issues.evidence: After first Delphes kill: 'free -h' showed 0B swap available. Two more attempts followed with minor variations before pivoting to Python analysis.

issues.label: CLEAR_LIMITATION_REPORTING
issues.description: The report provides an unusually thorough and honest accounting of all approximations, with quantitative estimates of their expected impact (e.g., '~10–20% bias from missing detector resolution', '~5% NLL correction not applied', '~1.5% b-mistag rate neglected').
issues.evidence: Report 'Notes on deviations from paper' section lists 5 specific deviations with magnitude estimates.

trajectory.overall_assessment: A strong run that demonstrates solid particle physics knowledge and engineering resourcefulness. The agent correctly set up the MSSM spectrum, generated and showered 50k events, obtained the NLO cross-section from Prospino, and implemented a faithful VZ signal region selection. The Delphes OOM failure was handled by writing a complete truth-level Python analysis — a substantial workaround that preserved the core physics. Final yields are 10–20% below reference, entirely consistent with the documented truth-level approximation. The main inefficiency was persisting with Delphes after clear OOM evidence, but this cost moderate time, not correctness. The artifacts (analysis script, report, datasets manifest) are well-documented and reproducible.
